message.text: `Revision.shows` is the new rule for whether a lens prompt showed a miss's lines, and `MissLines.saw` and `MissCause.read` both rely on it. It assumes, and its doc comment says, that "a prompt that carries the file's diff whole shows only the lines its hunks hold". The active enclosing-functions clauses say otherwise: at a level that reads `functions`, the change prompt also carries the head's whole function around each hunk of a TypeScript file, as numbered lines. Those levels include every built-in lens's `deep` level and the design lens's `careful` level. The telemetry `Stage` records only `shown` (whole diffs) and `read` (read_file lines). Nothing records the function blocks, so the rule never counts them as shown.

evidence.snippet:
if (covering.some((stage) => lines.saw(stage))) return "seen, not reported";
		return covering.some((stage) => stage.outcome === "completed") ? "never shown" : "cut short";

- At a level that reads `functions`, the change prompt carries the head's function around each hunk of a TypeScript file, after the diffs, each in a `function` block of its own with numbered lines.
- The compiler finds the bounds: TypeScript 7's native syntax tree, asked through `HeadProgram`, a virtual file system holding the head's text from git.
- A callback passed to a call has no name, so the named function around it holds the hunk. A deletion's anchor is the pair of lines it sits between, and a function holds it only when it holds both.
- Every other case, a file in another language, a hunk outside any function, a function past 250 lines, a file past 512 KiB or past the first 200 TypeScript files, and blocks and the not-shown listing past 64 KiB together, stays with the instruction: the lens reads the function with `read_file`.
- The instruction says so unconditionally: the lens reads with `read_file` every hunk that has no function block, whatever the reason.
const functions = settings.reads === "functions" ? await enclosing() : undefined;

explanation.what: `Revision.shows` is the new rule for whether a lens prompt showed a miss's lines, and `MissLines.saw` and `MissCause.read` both rely on it. It assumes, and its doc comment says, that "a prompt that carries the file's diff whole shows only the lines its hunks hold". The active enclosing-functions clauses say otherwise: at a level that reads `functions`, the change prompt also carries the head's whole function around each hunk of a TypeScript file, as numbered lines. Those levels include every built-in lens's `deep` level and the design lens's `careful` level. The telemetry `Stage` records only `shown` (whole diffs) and `read` (read_file lines). Nothing records the function blocks, so the rule never counts them as shown.
explanation.whatToDo: Count the enclosing-function blocks as shown. For example, record in the lens stage which function spans its prompt carried (beside `shown`) and make `MissLines.saw` test them. If that cannot be recorded, read a miss at a `functions` level that falls outside every hunk as `no record` instead of `never shown`. Correct the `Revision.shows` doc comment either way.
explanation.whyHere: This change turns the hunk-only test into a cause label printed in every `compare export` and totalled in `compare stats`. The design text the change adds says the label exists to pick the fix: a lens that never saw the line needs a different fix from one that saw it and stayed silent. A line the prompt carried inside a function block gets read `never shown` (or `cut short`). The fix it points to is showing the lens more, but the lens was in fact shown the line and missed it.

properties.failureScenario: A trust-boundary run at `deep` (LENS.md: `deep: { reads: functions }`) reviews a change whose only hunk in `src/user.ts` is lines 25–26. Those lines sit inside a 40-line function `load()` spanning lines 10–49. The change prompt carries the diff for `src/user.ts` whole, so `shown` holds the file. It also carries `load()` whole in a `function` block, because review.ts reads `enclosing()` when `settings.reads === "functions"`. Codex reports a defect at line 30, and the maintainer adjudicates it a valid miss. `melian compare export` then calls `MissLines.of("src/user.ts", [[30,30]], revision)`. `revision.shows` finds no head-side hunk on line 30, so `diffShows` is false. The lens did not read_file line 30, so `saw()` is false. The run completed, so `MissCause.read` returns `never shown`. The export prints `never shown`, and `compare stats` counts it under `First read "never shown"`, although the prompt showed line 30 to the lens. The correct read is `seen, not reported`, the case for a golden on the lens. The same happens for every design-lens run, since that lens reads functions at `careful`.
